title: kv-cache: memory manager tuning and spillover eviction prioritization
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: Production fleets observed increased tail latency and OOMs with mixed workloads. Root cause: GPU-resident KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal spillover prioritization. Motivation: reduce OOMs and tail latency without degrading throughput by making the memory manager fragmentation-aware and eviction hotness-aware. Summary: 1) compacting-aware allocator tracking free-region fragmentation and preferring allocations that minimize splits. 2) access-hotness score (decayed LRU-like) so spillover/eviction prefers cold segments. 3) multi-tier spillover prioritization: host-page spillover for large cold contiguous ranges, GPU-to-host spillover for fragmented small segments, immediate eviction only when critical. 4) exposes runtime knobs kv.memory.compaction_threshold and kv.spillover.priority_bias with fleet-derived defaults. 5) microbenchmarks, stress tests, and canary rollout plan. Changes confined to runtime/kv_cache with test harness updates.

review_comments: Elliot Nguyen: Nice overall shape. Two asks: (1) document complexity of free-region ops; (2) add an opt-out flag for customers during initial canary.
Priya Kapoor: Reply: Free-region ops are O(log m) on average using a per-GPU tree; added complexity notes in memory_manager.rs. Added kv.memory.disable_compaction flag and wired into rollout.
Marco Silva: Please emit 'kv.compaction_runs' and 'kv.spillover_bytes' metrics and verify host-page path has backpressure.

Priya Kapoor: Confirmed no public C ABI changes; added docs and included dedicated runners in second canary wave.
ci_checks: bench/kv-fragmentation: perf improved p99 -9% vs baseline
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: reduces fragmentation-driven OOMs and tail latency by introducing a compact-aware allocator, hotness-aware eviction, and smarter spillover prioritization. Exposes runtime knobs: kv.memory.compaction_threshold, kv.spillover.priority_bias. Backwards-compatible defaults retained.
testing: Unit and integration tests added. 48h staging stress suite and 24h 5% production canary with tracing. Benchmarks show p99 latency improvement and reduced rehydrate cost. Metrics added for compaction_runs and spillover_bytes.
notes: Follow-up: pair with continuous-batching (ENG-4410) to further reduce rehydrate cost; evaluate adaptive compaction trigger in a later PR.
canary_stream: Canary started 2024-11-07 10:00 UTC at 5% production; monitored until 2024-11-09 10:00 UTC with no rollback. Gradual ramp to 25% scheduled. Observed p99 latency down ~9-12% for mixed workloads, OOMs reduced from 18/day to 1/day in canary cluster, rehydrate cost reduced ~25%.
